issues.legal_issue: The destruction of a leased building does not determine the tenancy when the lease includes the land beneath the building and that land continues to exist.
material_facts: The appellant had rented a godown standing on part of a plot and had continuously paid rent and used the godown.
The respondent acquired the ownership interests in the plot, while the appellant’s leasehold interest was not acquired by the respondent.
The godown was demolished or collapsed, but the land beneath it remained.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy was not determined by the demolition or destruction of the godown. The ruling that the tenancy had lapsed was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 105, 108 and 111 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a lease transfers an interest in immovable property, and destruction of a building alone does not determine a lease when the land forming part of the subject matter continues to exist. Section 108(B)(e) gives the lessee an option to treat a lease as void in the specified circumstances; it does not make the lease automatically terminate. A lease of a building standing on land ordinarily comprises both the building and its site. The Court followed T. Lakshmipathi & Ors. v. R. Nithyananda Reddy & Ors., relying also on Section 5 of the Act and Raja Dhruv Dev Chand v. Raja Harmohinder Singh, and on the understanding of a building’s site in D.G. Gose & Co. (Agents) (P) Ltd. v. State of Kerala and Corporation of the City of Victoria v. Bishop of Vancouver Island. It overruled Vannattankandy Ibrayi v. Kunhabdulla Hajee to the extent it held that complete destruction of a building extinguished the tenancy in these circumstances.

rule.if: ordinary_property_lease and leased_structure_stood_on_land and structure_destroyed and land_site_remains

predicates.ordinary_property_lease: The dispute concerns a lease of immovable property governed by ordinary property-lease law rather than a special rent-law regime.
predicates.leased_structure_stood_on_land: The tenant leased a building or structure standing on land as the subject matter of the lease.
predicates.structure_destroyed: The leased building or structure was destroyed or demolished.
predicates.land_site_remains: The land on which the leased building or structure stood continues to exist.

issues.definition: When an ordinary property lease covers a structure standing on land, destruction of the structure does not end the tenancy if the land remains.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who succeeds in an appeal concerning the continuation of the tenancy may receive compensation instead of restoration of possession when the tenant has been out of possession for a long time.
material_facts: The appellant had been out of possession of the suit property for a long time.
The Court set aside the judgments that had held the tenancy had lapsed, but declined to direct restoration of possession.
The Court directed the respondent to pay compensation, with interest accruing if payment was not made within the specified time.
issues.conclusion: The respondent was directed to pay the appellant ₹20,00,000 as compensation instead of restoring possession; interest at 6% per annum would be payable from the date of judgment if payment was not made within two months.
issues.legal_principle: The Court made a case-specific remedial direction after concluding that the tenancy had not been determined, taking account of the appellant’s long absence from possession. It did not cite a statutory provision or earlier case as the basis for this compensation-in-lieu-of-restoration direction.

predicates.appellate_tenancy_dispute: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether a tenant’s lease or tenancy continues.
predicates.tenant_entitled_to_lease: The tenant’s lease or tenancy is found to have continued.
predicates.tenant_out_of_possession_long_term: The tenant has been out of possession for a long time.

issues.definition: In an appellate tenancy dispute, when the tenant’s lease continues but the tenant has been out of possession for a long time, compensation may be awarded instead of restoring possession.
